analysis.title: Jinko Holdings (JKS): Slight near-term margin relief likely to give way to renewed pressure into year-end
key_insights: GS keeps Sell on JKS and cuts the 12-month price target to $7 from $8. Price was $8.63 at the 30 Oct 2026 close, implying 18.9% downside.
3Q26 revenue was $2.03bn, below GSe $2.44bn and FactSet consensus $2.43bn. Module shipments fell qoq from 16.0GW to 15.0GW, below GSe of ~16.2GW and at the low end of the 15GW-17GW guidance range.
3Q26 gross margin was 12.3% vs GSe 6.9%, up 810bps qoq and 500bps yoy. Drivers were cost optimization, a favorable product mix and higher-margin ESS.
3Q26 EPS per ADS was ($0.48) vs GSe ($1.45) and consensus ($2.13). EBITDA was $157.2mn vs GSe $78.0mn.

Management believes module ASPs have bottomed and should stabilize, but expects 4Q26 gross margin pressure from a larger China shipment mix, legacy contracts signed earlier in the year, material costs and elevated logistics expenses.
4Q26 module shipment guidance is 16GW-18GW, below GSe of 18.6GW. FY2026 ESS shipment guidance is maintained at ~10 GWh on a proof-of-delivery basis.

ESS revenue-recognized volume is expected at ~6-7 GWh in 2026, including ~3 GWh in 4Q26, with ~7 GWh of cumulative shipments deferred into 2027 given a 6-12 month commissioning and revenue recognition cycle.

In 3Q26 JKS recognized 1.75 GWh of ESS as revenue, equal to all of FY25, and ESS posted its first positive quarterly operating profit. ESS gross margin is ~15%-20% vs ~10% for modules, but adds only ~100bps-200bps to consolidated gross margin.

Tiger Neo3.0 shipments exceeded 5 GW in 3Q26 at a ~US$0.01/W premium, ~30% of 3Q shipments and rising toward ~40% in 4Q26. Management expects ~40 GW of capacity meeting Level 1 national energy efficiency requirements by YE26. Tiger Neo5.0 all-black residential module will ramp gradually over two years.
Cash and restricted cash fell to $2.32bn from $2.50bn qoq. Net debt rose to $4.41bn from $4.12bn and total interest-bearing debt to ~$6.73bn from ~$6.62bn, with short-term debt at ~$2.29bn.
9M26 operating cash flow was ~$91mn vs ~($190mn) in 9M25. GS sees this as modest against $4.41bn net debt, with limited evidence of sustained deleveraging.
GS raises 2026E/2027E/2028E EBITDA to $429mn/$615mn/$734mn from $337mn/$637mn/$725mn, on higher gross margins in 2026. Revenue estimates fall 9%/6%/4% to $8.17bn/$10.92bn/$11.71bn.
2026E/2027E EPS (diluted) moves to ($4.20)/($0.21) from ($5.29)/($0.27). 2028E EPS rises to $2.29 from $1.94.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $7 from $8, based on 4.5x EV/EBITDA on Q5-Q8 EBITDA estimates and higher net debt. Margin relief in 3Q26 is expected to reverse in 4Q26 and leverage keeps rising.

sector_views.rationale: GS stays Sell on JKS. Module ASPs are said to have bottomed, but 4Q26 margins face pressure from China mix, legacy contracts, material and logistics costs.

earnings_insights: JKS 3Q26 (reported, quarter ended Sep-26): revenue $2,031mn vs GSe $2,441mn (-17%) and FactSet consensus $2.43bn. Gross margin 12.3% vs GSe 6.9%. EBITDA $157.2mn vs GSe $78.0mn. EPS per ADS (basic) ($0.48) reported vs GSe ($1.45) and consensus ($2.13). Diluted EPS per ADS ($0.93).
3Q26 operating income was ($11.9mn) reported vs GSe ($141.1mn). Subsidy income was $57.5mn vs GSe $29.7mn. Net income was ($25.4mn) vs GSe ($76.7mn).
3Q26 operating cash flow was $118.8mn and capex $260.0mn, giving free cash flow to equity of ($141.2mn).
4Q26 guidance: module shipments 16GW-18GW (GSe 18.6GW). FY2026 ESS shipments ~10 GWh (proof-of-delivery basis).

GS estimates (not reported): 2026E EBITDA $428.6mn, 2027E $615.2mn, 2028E $734.4mn. 2026E diluted EPS ($4.20), 2027E ($0.21), 2028E $2.29. Quarterly EPS estimates: ($0.93) for 9/26, ($0.78) for 12/26E, ($0.76) for 3/27E, ($0.62) for 6/27E.

trade_ideas.description: Sell rating on JKS with 12-month price target of $7.00
trade_ideas.rationale: Renewed 4Q26 gross margin pressure, weak shipment guidance and rising net debt outweigh the 3Q26 margin recovery.
trade_ideas.risk: Faster cost declines, lower poly pricing, a reduction in or removal of global solar trade restrictions, capacity rationalization, and lower capex.

tension_points.bull_case: 3Q26 gross margin rose to 12.3% from lower costs, richer mix and higher-margin ESS, which posted its first positive quarterly operating profit. Management believes module ASPs have bottomed and Tiger Neo3.0 share is rising toward ~40% of shipments.
tension_points.bear_case: Management expects 4Q26 gross margin pressure from a greater China mix, legacy contracts, material costs and logistics. Shipment guidance is below GSe, ESS adds only ~100bps-200bps to consolidated margin, and net debt rose to $4.41bn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Faster cost declines, lower poly pricing, or removal of global solar trade restrictions would undermine the Sell view, per the report's key risks.
